groups.title: Cardinal-numeral foundation and count kind
groups.proposal: Build cardinal numerals as typed absolutive-state NNCs in the vigesimal system. Preserve numeral Sources for later NNC and VNC embedding, distinguish ordinary count from gross or total count by the ix matrix, derive subject-number behavior from count kind and referent animacy, and treat the five counting sets as productive typed classifier structures rather than inventories of example nouns.
groups.writingJob: Create a typed cardinal-numeral Source with numeral value, count kind, referent facts, and compatible counting-set analysis; derive ordinary versus ix gross structure, absolutive-state NNC behavior, subject-number restrictions, and later embed eligibility through the canonical numeral owner.
groups.readingJob: Show vigesimal value, ordinary or gross count, ix totality structure, subject animacy and number consequence, selected counting set, embed eligibility, and examples as evidence rather than admission lists.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended numeral value and ordinary versus gross count. The user chooses a counting set only where the referent is genuinely compatible with more than one. The application derives vigesimal structure, state, subject-number consequences, and embed behavior.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse the cardinal-numeral NNC Source operation and canonical NNC owner. Do not add decimal decomposition, manual ix, subject-number repair, example-noun, or stem-whitelist controls.

groups.title: One and the cē/cem Source shapes
groups.proposal: Represent one with the fuller typed nounstem Source cem. Derive free cē by final-m loss plus compensatory length, retain cem before a following morpheme, apply boundary assimilation automatically, use m-eh with a plural subject, and allow the same numeral Source to enter ordinary NNC compounds or incorporated-adverb VNC compounds without using the listed compounds and verbs as route gates.
groups.writingJob: Preserve the morphemic Source cem, derive cē versus cem from free or embedded position, apply nasal assimilation and plural m-eh canonically, and pass the typed numeral Source into compatible compound-NNC and incorporated-adverb VNC owners.
groups.readingJob: Show the fuller cem Source, free cē realization, compensatory length, plural m-eh, boundary assimilation, NNC or VNC embedding, contextual adverbial readings, and non-authorizing examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended value and a licensed NNC-versus-VNC operation when both are genuinely intended. The application derives cē or cem, vowel length, assimilation, plural marking, and the compound boundary.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add cē-versus-cem, vowel-length, final-m, assimilation, plural-dyad, or example-compound controls. Preserve typed Source shape and use the existing NNC and VNC compound pathways.

groups.title: Two, three, four, and their positional shapes
groups.proposal: Build two, three, and four from typed pronominal numeral Sources ōme, ēyi, and nāhui. Derive ordinary plural n plus the licensed t-in or silent number dyad, form gross count with ix, and select free or embedded allomorphs from the exact boundary environment: ōme or ōm, the licensed ēyi family including embed ē/yē/ēx, and nāhu before vowels versus nāuh before consonants. Preserve optional initial-y and other documented variants only where the typed Source leaves a real alternative.
groups.writingJob: Derive number marking, gross-count ix structure, and every free-versus-embed allomorph of two through four from typed value, Source analysis, vowel quantity, and the following boundary while preserving any genuinely licensed spelling or realization alternative.
groups.readingJob: Show value, pronominal Source, ordinary or gross count, plural dyads, ix structure, free and embedded shapes, following-vowel or consonant evidence, y and x alternations, assimilation, and examples as evidence rather than a stem list.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the value, ordinary versus gross meaning, and only a genuinely unresolved licensed variant. The application derives plural structure, ix, truncation, y or x behavior, nāhu versus nāuh, assimilation, and compound placement from the typed Source and boundary.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add manual truncation, ix, y-loss, y-to-x, vowel-versus-consonant, assimilation, or number-dyad controls. Do not authorize the route by example identity.

groups.title: Five through nine and their internal composition
groups.proposal: Preserve five as the typed derived nounstem mā-cu-ī-l and build six through nine as the productive chicua/chiuc/chic plus one-through-four numeral structure. Derive boundary-conditioned embed shapes, assimilation, ordinary plural marking, and ix gross count automatically while keeping historical derivation and translations as reading evidence.
groups.writingJob: Build five through nine from their typed morphemic Sources, preserve internal boundaries and vowel quantity, derive the correct chicua-family allomorph and basic-numeral matrix, and reuse ordinary and gross cardinal inflection.
groups.readingJob: Show numerical composition, historical Source, embed and matrix, boundary-conditioned allomorphy, ordinary or gross count, plural marking, and examples without turning the four documented compounds into a route inventory.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the value and count meaning. The application derives the internal five-plus-x composition, allomorph, boundaries, assimilation, ix, and number marking.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add chicua/chiuc/chic, internal matrix, assimilation, or example-number controls; derive them from value and morphemic boundary.

groups.title: Ten, fifteen, and the gross-count possessive formation
groups.proposal: Build ten and fifteen from typed mahtlāc and caxtōl nounstems, derive their ordinary and ix gross forms and animate plural marking, and license the exceptional possessive-state gross-count formation only with the required plural or plural-referent possessor facts while preserving the documented nonanimate ti/tin uncertainty as evidence or a real licensed variant.
groups.writingJob: Execute ten and fifteen through the canonical numeral owner, preserve their morphemic Sources, derive ix and number marking, and enforce the special gross-count possessive participant restrictions without extending possessive state to ordinary numerals.
groups.readingJob: Show ten or fifteen Source structure, ordinary or gross count, absolutive versus exceptional possessive state, possessor animacy and plurality, ti/tin evidence, and non-authorizing examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses value, gross meaning, and possessive state when that meaning is intended; a ti-versus-tin choice appears only if the typed nonanimate Source preserves both. The application enforces possessor and number compatibility.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add general numeral possession, ix, possessor-number repair, or example-stem controls. Keep the exceptional route typed and narrow.

groups.title: Multiples of twenty, four hundred, and eight thousand
groups.proposal: Form higher vigesimal orders by embedding any typed numeral value from one through nineteen before the fixed typed matrices pōhualli, tzontli, or xiquipilli. Derive the multiplier and total value, preserve each matrix's Source and meaning, and keep secondary lexical readings such as many or mockingbird separate from productive numeral structure.
groups.writingJob: Build typed multiplier-plus-order compound nounstems for twenty, four hundred, and eight thousand, derive value and general-use embed shape, preserve all internal morphemic boundaries, and pass the Result through ordinary or gross numeral inflection.
groups.readingJob: Show multiplier, order matrix, computed value, Source meaning, embedded shape, ordinary or gross count, secondary lexical readings, and examples as proof rather than allowed-value lists.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended value or order meaning. The application decomposes the value, selects the order matrix and embed shape, computes the total, and derives boundaries and inflection.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add matrix spelling, multiplication, manual embed-shape, or example-value controls. Keep lexicalized nonnumeral readings typed separately.

groups.title: Conjoined numerals, recursion, and downgraded embeds
groups.proposal: Compose higher and lower numeral NNC Results as an ordered, conjunctorless and recursively nestable conjunction whose rightward conjunct contains short om. Also allow the licensed conjunctive-compound realization and downgrade a complete conjunction to a bound embed by deleting only the rightmost number position before a higher-order matrix. Preserve long ōm 'two' versus short om 'additional' and forbid same-matrix numeral conjunction.
groups.writingJob: Recapture owner-issued numeral Results, order them from higher to lower, add and assimilate short om on rightward conjuncts, preserve recursive hierarchy, realize the licensed compound alternative, and downgrade a full conjunction to a typed embed without losing its internal Sources.
groups.readingJob: Show conjunct values and order, short om versus long ōm, assimilation, recursion, conjunctive-compound alternative, downgraded rank, deleted rightmost number position, outer order matrix, forbidden same-matrix conjunction, and scribal evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses separate-clause versus conjunctive-compound form only where both are intended and grammatical. The application derives order, om, assimilation, recursion, downgrading, deleted number position, and matrix compatibility.
groups.controlPolicy: Require canonical numeral Results for composition. Do not accept typed strings, formulas, example spellings, manual om, deletion, bracketing, or multiplication as authority.

groups.title: Rock, row, thing, and maize-cob counting sets
groups.proposal: Build the four derived unit-count sets by embedding an open typed basic numeral before the selected te, pān, tla-man, or ōlō classifier matrix. Preserve referent compatibility without rigid example categories, omit the classifier on rightward conjuncts, derive each set's number behavior, permit recursive compounding, and enforce the maize-cob set's through-nineteen limit with typed tlamic continuation for twenty through thirty-nine.
groups.writingJob: Apply a compatible typed classifier matrix to a basic numeral Source, derive boundary shape and number marking, preserve classifier omission in rightward conjunction, allow canonical compound continuation, and enforce the cob-set value range and owner-issued tlamic prerequisite.
groups.readingJob: Show classifier matrix and meaning, referent compatibility, value, boundary realization, subject number, gross count, conjunction behavior, recursive embedding, cob limit, tlamic continuation, and flexible usage evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a classifier only where the referent allows more than one counting analysis. The application derives its matrix, boundary, inflection, conjunction behavior, recursion, range limits, and required continuation.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not create a referent-noun whitelist or manual classifier-omission, boundary, plural, or tlamic controls. A typed referent analysis may constrain but examples never authorize.

groups.title: Special counting sets for groups of twenty
groups.proposal: Count groups of twenty with productive typed classifier matrices tecpān, ipil, or quimil according to the intended grouping and compatible referent facts. Embed the basic multiplier Source, compute the score value, and preserve ordinary numeral conjunction for the remainder without treating listed people, animals, houses, rocks, blankets, paper, tortillas, or hides as route whitelists.
groups.writingJob: Build multiplier-plus-special-score compounds with the selected typed matrix, preserve the exact morphemic Source, derive total value and boundary shape, and continue through canonical numeral conjunction for lower remainders.
groups.readingJob: Show group-of-twenty meaning, classifier matrix, compatible referent analysis, multiplier, computed value, boundaries, remainder conjunction, and examples as evidence only.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses a special score classifier only when the intended grouping or referent leaves more than one grammatical option. The application derives multiplier, total, boundaries, and remainder structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add example-referent lists, manual score multiplication, embed-shape, or remainder-order controls.

groups.title: Affinity and distributive-varietal numeral reduplication
groups.proposal: Apply the established nounstem affinity and distributive-varietal reduplication meanings to typed numeral Sources. Derive ordinary first-part scope, double scope in seven through nine, mahtlāc matrix scope, and all-conjunct scope in conjoined numerals from internal morphemic structure while preserving vowel length versus glottal stop.
groups.writingJob: Recapture a typed numeral Source, apply the chosen grammatical reduplication meaning at every structurally required target, preserve boundaries and vowel quantity, and reuse canonical number, classifier, and conjunction realization.
groups.readingJob: Show affinity versus distribution or variety, continuity versus separation, reduplication targets, vowel length or glottal evidence, double and all-conjunct scope, number marking, classifier structure, and examples.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses affinity versus distributive-varietal meaning only where context does not settle it. The application derives the target positions and realization from the numeral's internal structure.
groups.controlPolicy: Do not add embed, matrix, double, or all-conjunct scope switches; those are automatic structural consequences.

groups.title: Approximately, more, and supplementary oc cē
groups.proposal: Modify an owner-issued numeral NNC with canah, quēn, ahzo quēn, or oc according to the intended approximation or additional-count meaning, and allow the complete sentence oc cē to function as a supplementary subject through the canonical supplementation owner without converting English else expressions into new grammar.
groups.writingJob: Recapture the numeral NNC, add the selected licensed modifier in its canonical position, preserve its scope, and pass oc cē as a complete owner-issued supplement when participant and reference conditions license it.
groups.readingJob: Show modifier identity and scope, approximate or additional meaning, complete numeral Result, supplementary-subject relation, negative or interrogative context, and English else as translation evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended approximation or more meaning and a real supplementation relation. Modifier placement and eligible supplementation behavior are automatic.
groups.controlPolicy: Reuse sentence-particle and supplementation owners. Do not add English-gloss, else, interrogative, negative, or example-sentence route controls.

groups.title: Measure NNCs and measured-NNC composition
groups.proposal: Build measure NNCs by embedding an open typed numeral Source before any compatible typed measure matrix, preserving whether the Result expresses amount or length. Combine the owner-issued measure NNC with the owner-issued measured-thing NNC only through the later adjectival-modification relation in which the measure is principal, without using the listed mouthful, spoonful, branchful, ovenful, grip, or body-length matrices as a whitelist.
groups.writingJob: Construct a typed numeral-plus-measure compound NNC, preserve both morphemic Sources and boundary, derive ordinary NNC inflection, and recapture the complete measure and measured-thing Results in the canonical principal-plus-modifier composition.
groups.readingJob: Show numeral embed, measure matrix and meaning, amount or length reading, boundary and Result class, principal measure clause, measured-thing modifier, later lesson dependency, and examples as non-authorizing evidence.
groups.decisionSplit: The user chooses the intended compatible measure Source and, where needed, amount versus length meaning. The application derives compound structure and the measure-as-principal composition relation.
groups.controlPolicy: Keep measure Sources productively open. Do not create example-measure whitelists, manual boundary, Result-class, principal-clause, or formula controls.
